title: Los Angeles-based firm breaks ground on $15B data center in Hudspeth County
key_facts: Los Angeles-based Kaufman & Company and other companies broke ground on a $15 billion data centre facility near Desert Haven, Hudspeth County, Texas, on Wednesday (7 Oct 2026).
Hudspeth County Judge Joanna MacKenzie said none of the local authorities were notified before groundbreaking and that she heard rumours on Thursday 8 Oct.
The campus is planned on about 24,000 acres of desert land with dome-like structures and a well connected to an aquifer under the property.
Boise-based ServerDomes says the campus is planned to generate 350 MW, enough for at least 100,000 homes, and that water is drawn once during setup and then recycled in a closed loop.
MacKenzie says the planners apologised for little communication and agreed to present at the 27 Oct meeting.
Texas counties have no zoning power to regulate land use on private property.
quote_evidence: "However, when you're talking about a project that could potentially impact locals by way of use of power and water source, I do think that local government should be included in that conversation."
The planned data center campus sits on private property, and counties in Texas do not have zoning power to regulate land use like cities.
why_it_matters_hint: A $15 billion campus started on private desert land with local officials uninformed and no county zoning power.
notes: KTSM is the original reporter; the EverythingLubbock page is a Nexstar copy and its KTSM original link was not found. Figures are company claims relayed by the county judge.
